### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/permissions/field-level-security.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/index.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/permissions/sharing-rules.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/plugins/packages.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/ui/forms.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **4** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/implementation-status.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v15.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-6.mdx`  _(via getReadFilter (symbol, a method of class SecurityPlugin))_
- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-0.mdx`  _(via SecurityPlugin (symbol, a top-level class))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 72 pages)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **28** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `427878d9328cfb487290467052ff7086d318e329` — the merge of head `2a8d0d5b4132ea6dacecbb0bdb73f1dfc59b5ad1` into base `601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 427878d9328cfb487290467052ff7086d318e329 && git checkout 427878d9328cfb487290467052ff7086d318e329
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103 2a8d0d5b4132ea6dacecbb0bdb73f1dfc59b5ad1 && git checkout -B drift-repro 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103 && git merge --no-ff 2a8d0d5b4132ea6dacecbb0bdb73f1dfc59b5ad1

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 601b258d72cc6dde7e838a79d20eef18ba381103` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4c31b7cc93dc2ca485f32bc3c17f1c09b0f3164b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: docs/adr/0139-engine-internal-semi-join-leaf-readable-parent-ids.md + packages/objectql/src/engine.ts (`composeReadableIdsAtBoundary`, `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`, `readableIdsScopeOf`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts (`getReadFilter`, `computeDelegatedReadFilter`, `resolveSharingReadFilter`, `canReadObject` / `objectReadAdmission`, `resolveOperationPrincipals`, the read middleware's steps 2.5 / 2.6 / 3, `computeRlsFilter`, `computeControlledByParentFilter`, `collectRLSPolicies`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/explain-engine.ts (`resolveDelegatorContext`), packages/plugins/plugin-sharing/src/sharing-plugin.ts (the read middleware's two `buildReadFilter` legs) and sharing-service.ts (`buildReadFilter`, `shouldBypass`), packages/spec/src/contracts/security-service.ts (`getReadFilter` and `canReadObject` docblocks), packages/spec/src/data/readable-ids.ts, docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md D10, and every `getReadFilter` caller on `origin/main` (`4d991588f`): packages/services/service-analytics/src/plugin.ts (the `getReadScope` bridge and the `admitObjectRead` bridge beside it) plus the leaf consumers' probe routing in packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/parent-record-read-gate.ts and packages/services/service-storage/src/attachment-access-hooks.ts.

Inputs: card #25009 (body, the dispatch claim 6305174176, the dev report 6306430776); ruling 6303721609 on #24932; PR #25032 body, its 11-file list and the net diff `origin/main...4c31b7cc9` (812 / 107, merge base `73432299c`, which the branch carries; `origin/main` is two commits past it, neither in these regions); the 38 check-runs on the head, read once at 02:25Z. `reviewFace` hits: the ADR alone; the scope above is the widening this record chose because the amended D5.1 describes a runtime security boundary.

### ① Derived judgments

**The governed text against the code it describes — each claim named right or wrong.**

- D5 retitled, D5.1 "composed, not refused": RIGHT. `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses` no longer takes a context (engine.ts 6245–6250); the delegated throw is gone; D5.2 (object-scoped middleware parent) and D5.3 (other datasource) keep their named refusals with the same envelope and text (6254–6263).
- "asks both halves with the delegated context exactly as it stands, `onBehalfOf` intact": RIGHT. `readableIdsScopeOf` passes `context` unchanged to `canReadObject(parent, context)` and `getReadFilter(parent, context)` (6273–6282); the objectql pin reads the link off both calls.
- "`canReadObject` already intersected the object half": RIGHT on `main` already — `canReadObject` resolves the delegator once (6453–6460) and `objectReadAdmission` arms 4 and 6 ask the capability gate and the `find` grant of the delegator's sets too.
- "`getReadFilter` now answers the row half through `computeDelegatedReadFilter`, the six layers the engine middleware chain ANDs into a delegated `find` of P": RIGHT, primitive for primitive. The chain's read path (security middleware step 3, 4396–4425) ANDs `computeLayeredRlsFilter` layer0+layer1 and `computeControlledByParentFilter` for the principal and, when `delegatorSets` resolved, the same two over `delegatorContext`; `computeRlsFilter` is exactly `andComposeLayers(layer0, layer1)` over `computeLayeredRlsFilter` (7651–7660). plugin-sharing's middleware (sharing-plugin.ts 1288–1316) ANDs `buildReadFilter(object, exec)` and `buildReadFilter(object, {...exec, userId: delegator, onBehalfOf: undefined, __readScope: exec.__delegatorReadScope})`. `computeDelegatedReadFilter` (6033–6078) makes the same six calls with the same sets (`resolvePermissionSetsForContext` reads positions + permissions, not the link, so the principal's sets are the ceiling in both paths), the same delegator context (`resolveDelegatorContext`, the one resolver), the same depths (step 2.6's `intersectDelegatedScope(getDeclaredScope(ceiling), getEffectiveScope(delegator))` for the agent leg, `getEffectiveScope(delegator)` for the delegator leg — `depthFor` at 2945–2949 is the same two evaluator calls), and `buildReadFilter` reads only `userId`, guest, `__readScope` and `shouldBypass` (isSystem / bypass objects), none of which differ between the two spellings. The other three `registerMiddleware` sites in plugin-security (4551 position-catalog, 4820 bootstrap replay, 4843 org-admin grant) narrow no read, so six is the whole read-narrowing set.
- "the engine derives no second intersection": RIGHT. The chain intersects nothing beyond those six on a read; the engine composes what it is answered and marks it `'policy'`.
- "the closed doors are the chain's": RIGHT, see the security answer below.
- "`resolveDelegatorContext` in explain-engine.ts", "`collectRLSPolicies` / `isDelegatedPrincipalLeg` keeps the ceiling's silence from collecting the object default": RIGHT (explain-engine.ts export; security-plugin.ts 406–409, 9717).
- D6 amended with the ruling quoted verbatim, the order (b)(i) → (b)(ii) → (c), the two things not taken (A stop-gap, the predicate removal), "ADR-0055 §2 (b) stands until the switch; ADR-0055 moves only in that switch's edit": RIGHT against 6303721609 items 1–4; the ADR edits ADR-0055 and ADR-0090 nowhere. "Leaves unchanged" and the E2 row carry the same.
- The `getReadFilter` contract docblock (security-service.ts 384–387) still holds unchanged: it promises the deny filter "on a path that cannot compute the delegator intersection", a condition this head no longer meets, so no spec text moves. No exported signature changes in either package (`resolveSharingReadFilter`'s `depth` and `refuseUncomposableReadableIdsClasses`'s dropped parameter are both private); `packages/spec` untouched, no generated artifact owed.
- `readable-ids.ts`: the sentinel-by-identity contract is honoured by the new branch (every deny returns `RLS_DENY_FILTER` by reference; the leaf's `scope === RLS_DENY_FILTER` test at 6287 fires).

**The security question, consumer by consumer.** On `main`, `getReadFilter` answered the deny sentinel for every on-behalf-of context (the removed `[#2852]` block); on this head it answers the D10 intersection. Runtime call sites of `getReadFilter` on `origin/main`, by a strict `.getReadFilter(` sweep over every non-test source: exactly two (security-plugin.ts 2121 is the registration, not a consumer).

1. **The engine's `ReadableIds` leaf** (`engine.ts` 6282): does a delegated caller now read more than the engine's own delegated `find` chain admits? **No.** The leaf's scope for parent P = `canReadObject(P)` (object-level, both legs) ∧ the six-layer row scope above, which is row for row what a delegated `find(P)` runs under; and the leaf sits inside a `find` of the child that itself already passed the chain under the same delegated context, so it only narrows. Pinned on the real stack by rows (`readable-ids-delegated-compose.test.ts`: `c_both`, `c_shared` only; `find` and `count` agree; the parity pin compares `getReadFilter`'s scope with the delegated direct read). Live traffic: none — every shipped consumer still routes a delegated caller to its bounded probe (`isDelegatedCaller` at parent-record-read-gate.ts 451 for activity / ledger / comments / reactions, attachment-access-hooks.ts 1020 for attachments), so no leaf is written for a delegated caller today.
2. **The analytics raw-SQL / dataset path** (`service-analytics/src/plugin.ts` 672, the `getReadScope` auto-bridge): does a delegated caller now read more than the chain admits? **No.** The same door bridges `admitObjectRead` to `canReadObject` (plugin.ts ~798), so a delegated analytics read is object admission intersected ∧ the six-layer rows — the chain's own two questions. It widens relative to `main`'s deny-everything, by design and by the ruling, and never past a delegated direct read. Latent, not live: ADR-0090 D10's note says an agent principal is produced at the `/mcp` OAuth door alone, and no MCP / AI tool names analytics.
3. No other consumer exists (the lint rule text, the audit matrix note and the docblocks mention the name only; `scripts/analytics-reconcile/boot.ts` supplies its own stub provider).

**Fails closed exactly as the chain does?** Yes, in every case, with the shape the scope path owns: the chain throws (403 `PERMISSION_DENIED` or the find fails), the scope path answers the deny sentinel by identity, which the leaf turns into `$in: []` and analytics into zero rows. Case by case against `resolveOperationPrincipals` (8903–8947) and step 2.5: principal resolves no set → chain deny baseline / new `RLS_DENY_FILTER` (6037); delegator missing → chain 403 / new `canReadObject` false and the sentinel with the D10 invariant sentence logged (6041–6049); delegator resolves no set → chain step 2.5 `checkObjectPermission([])` false → 403 / new sentinel (6052) and `objectReadAdmission` arm 6 false; a throw in `resolvePermissionSetsForContext`, `buildContextForUser`, `getObjectSecurityMeta`, either `computeRlsFilter`, either `resolveSharingReadFilter` → propagates to `getReadFilter`'s catch → sentinel (5926–5938); a throw that still escaped → the engine's own `readableIdsScopeOf` catch → `$in: []`. `resolveDelegatorContext`'s third arm (`none`) is unreachable on both paths (both branch on `onBehalfOf.userId` first) and the new guard `del.kind !== 'resolved'` denies it anyway. Order matches the chain's prologue: `isSystem` bypass, then the principal-less refusal, then the delegated branch.

**Pins.** The objectql suite's old refusal pin is replaced by five cases (each verb asks both halves with the link intact; a middleware-written leaf composes; `canReadObject` false / sentinel / throw on either half ⇒ `$in: []`; D5.2 and D5.3 refuse with code and status, no driver call, service unasked; a control without the link). The five respelled plugin-security pins keep their assertions and now name the branch a `sys_user`-less rig actually reaches (a delegator who does not exist); `default-report-sink.test.ts` reads the exact D10 sentence the missing-delegator line keeps verbatim. Ablation legs A and B each red the expected pins and restored clean, per the report.

**Check-runs on the head, as read once at 02:25Z:** 38 runs, 0 `failure`; 24 `success` (Build Core, Lint · ESLint, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · CI release & engine gates, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, the three scoped lint legs, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Check Changeset, Check PR Size, Governed Surface Queue Guard, the claim / single-writer / part-of checks, Check Documentation Links, Dogfood Regression Gate, Auto Label, filter, flag-docs); 8 `skipped` (opt-in and full-battery jobs); 10 `in_progress` (Test Core 1–6/6, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · workspace, Lint · repo & tooling gates). Not polled. The required contexts are therefore not all concluded at this read; this record is the contract-tier review of record for the head and is not a landing record — `docs/adr/**` is Tier H, so the landing waits on the maintainer's approval and on every check green.

### ② Semver level

`.changeset/25009-readable-ids-delegated-compose.md`: `@objectstack/objectql` minor, `@objectstack/plugin-security` minor — RIGHT. Exactly the two packages whose source changed; `plugin-audit`, `service-storage`, `spec` untouched and absent. Minor is the level of a capability added with no public signature change and no authorable surface moved; it matches the precedent the changeset cites (the ADR-0139 E2 and E5 landings). The body states Before / Now / What a reader sees / Unchanged accurately against the code (the analytics door's widening from deny to intersection is named; the consumers' unchanged routing is named).

`Clause-②: no` — RIGHT and consistent across the PR body, the changeset body and the dispatch claim: no spec key, schema or authorable accept set changes; the runtime read-scope change is the ruling's, as the claim states. No `(widening)` / `(narrowing)` arm, so no ADR-0087 marker is owed. `Check Changeset` success on the head.

1. Worktree takeover with the inherited hunks committed as a restore point before verification, no stash — answered: the process the dispatch set; every inherited hunk is re-verified at this head.

4. `check-engine-split-ratio --days 90` refused on the shallow clone — answered: a push / schedule metric, not a PR gate; its self-test row passed.
5. The derived-gate loop moved to background, 12 families run twice, reconciled on the deduplicated record — answered: a reporting artefact, no gate verdict depends on it.
6. Ablation leg A refused once by the tool and respelled — answered: nothing ran on the refused attempt, restore proven.
7. Report keys outside the role file's template — answered: additive.
8. The inherited WIP's red `default-report-sink` pin fixed by keeping the D10 sentence verbatim rather than loosening the pin — answered: the right direction (the assertion is unchanged; the sentence is in the branch a bare instance reaches).
9. Worktree removed after the report — answered: the branch holds every commit (three pushes, no force).

**Out-of-scope findings, each answered or escalated:**
- (a) The six consumers' up-front `'delegated-caller'` probe routing is now a residue of the refusal this PR removes; "carrier: none yet, noted, not filed". Answered as to this PR: a consumer switch is not this card's scope and leaving it is what keeps the shipped surface unchanged. ESCALATED to the dispatching seat: the amended D5.1 now states, in governed text, that the routing "is retired per consumer on its own card", and no such card exists — file the carrier (one card, or one per consumer, serial after #25010 in the same regions) so the ADR's sentence names a card that is real, before or at the landing.
- (b) The #24932 measured difference (2) (child read without object-level read on the master) — answered: card (c)'s question by the ruling; untouched here, correctly.

**Card (c) scope (#24932), held:** the two existing `computeControlledByParentFilter` call sites in the middleware and the one in the non-delegated `getReadFilter` are byte-unchanged; the id-list pre-scan (`ql.find(rel.master, …, isSystem)`) is unchanged; ADR-0055 is not in the file list. The delegated path adds two callers of that unchanged mechanism (principal and delegator legs), which is the parity the chain already has — not a switch, and inside card (b)(i). The ruling's item 3 (the HotCRM-scale 500 stays until (b) lands) is unaffected.

**Nits for the maintainer's Tier H read of the ADR, no verdict weight:** the "Open items" list still carries `O5 — whether … becomes a seventh consumer (D6)` without noting it is answered (the bullet points at D6, which now holds the verbatim ruling; a three-word tail would close the loop).
